//: Hand-written skill descriptions. sync-skills.mjs PREFERS these over auto-extraction. Add an entry whenever the auto-extracted description reads badly - description quality is the whole routing mechanism in Claude Code. Keys must match a directory under .cursor/skills/.
flutter-widget-gen: Generates a single reusable, presentation-only Flutter widget (card, button variant, list tile, empty/error state) matching this repo's existing widget conventions, with a const constructor, accessibility Semantics where needed, and a widget test. Use when asked to build a new reusable UI piece.
flutter-screen-gen: Generates a full Flutter screen in one pass: the screen widget, its backing Riverpod AsyncNotifier/Notifier, and the go_router route registration, handling loading/error/empty/data states explicitly. Use when asked to build a new screen or page.
flutter-provider-gen: Scaffolds a Riverpod Notifier or AsyncNotifier (codegen @riverpod style or manual, matching the repo's existing convention) that owns state and orchestrates repository calls via AsyncValue.guard. Use when asked to add state management, a provider, or a notifier.
flutter-repository-gen: Generates the data layer for a resource: an abstract repository interface, its API-client-backed implementation with typed error mapping, and the provider binding, so the application layer only depends on the interface. Use when asked to add a repository, API client, or data source.
flutter-model-gen: Generates an immutable freezed + json_serializable data class with JSON (de)serialization, correct @JsonKey mapping for API field names, and a round-trip test. Use when asked to add a model, entity, or DTO.
flutter-route-gen: Registers a new go_router route (path, name, builder, path parameters, auth redirect guard) in the app's router configuration, including nesting under an existing ShellRoute if applicable. Use when asked to add a route or wire navigation to a screen.
flutter-test-gen: Backfills widget, Notifier, or repository tests onto existing Flutter code using ProviderScope overrides, ProviderContainer, and mocktail/mockito fakes, covering loading/error/empty states and asserting behavior rather than implementation. Use when asked to add test coverage to existing code.
flutter-l10n-gen: Adds localization keys to every .arb locale file with ICU placeholders and metadata, flags locales needing human translation, and replaces literal strings with generated AppLocalizations accessors. Use when asked to localize or internationalize new user-facing strings.
flutter-architecture-audit: Read-only audit for layering violations against feature-first/layered architecture conventions - business logic in widgets, data-layer classes imported by presentation, misplaced provider scope, cross-feature boundary leaks. Use when asked to review or audit the app's architecture.
flutter-performance-audit: Read-only scan for common Flutter jank causes: missing const, over-broad ref.watch causing unnecessary rebuilds, ListView/Column used instead of .builder for long lists, unmanaged image caching, and expensive work inside build(). Use when asked about performance, jank, or rebuild issues.
flutter-accessibility-audit: Read-only audit for screen-reader support (Semantics labels on icon-only controls), minimum 48x48 tap target size, text contrast candidates, and unlabeled form fields. Use when asked to review or audit accessibility.
flutter-dependency-audit: Read-only review of pubspec.yaml for unused packages, stale exact-pinned versions, duplicate-purpose packages (e.g. both dio and http), and dev-only codegen packages misplaced in dependencies. Use when asked to audit or clean up dependencies.
feature-trace: Traces how an existing screen or user flow actually works today - route to screen widget, providers watched, Notifiers behind them, repository calls, and the underlying API/data source - so changes are based on the real code, not a guess. Use when asked how a screen or flow works.
impact-analysis: Determines the blast radius of a proposed change before it's made - every widget, provider, repository, route, and test that references the changed symbol, classified as breaking/behavioral/cosmetic, including golden-test and generated-code impact. Use before editing existing code, or when asked what breaks if something changes.
work-breakdown: Decomposes a feature, bug, or refactor into a task board sized so each task finishes in one agent session - presents vertical/horizontal/risk-first slicing options with tradeoffs, then enforces max 8 files and max 2 layers per task with a Verify command. Use when asked to break down, split, or plan out work.
release-safety: Plans how a mobile change reaches users via staged Play Console/App Store Connect rollout and feature flags with an owner and expiry, and defines a rollback plan that's explicit about what a store rollback does not undo. Use when asked about rollout, staged release, feature flags, or rollback for a mobile app.
production-readiness-review: The Go/No-Go gate before a Flutter release ships - checks crash reporting is wired and active in release builds, offline/error-state handling per screen, and the store submission checklist (privacy policy, permission usage strings, data-safety label accuracy). Use when asked whether a release or feature is ready to ship.
repo-discovery: Scans a Flutter repository's pubspec.yaml, lib/ structure, and actual state-management/routing/testing conventions in use, and writes the structural map other skills and context-sync read from. Use at the start of a session in an unmapped repo.
context-sync: Populates and refreshes the memory-bank's Tier 1 files (techContext.md, progress.md, activeContext.md) from repo-discovery's scan and current git state, without overwriting human-authored Tier 2 standards. Use when memory-bank is missing or stale.
